Experiment-Agentic-Flow/mepworkspace.purpose: Angular/Nx monorepo for MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing) solutions - dozens of apps (hcui, ecui, livecount, fabui, sxui, analytics-portal, admin-assist-portal, asset-iq-portal, ...) and shared libraries under libs/, organized by domain.

projects.name: admin-assist-portal
projects.purpose: This project is the main administrative portal application within the MEP workspace, providing user-facing capabilities to search distributor branches, configure integrations, manage ERP registrations, and extract reporting data. Operating as an application-level app shell, it orchestrates and composes lazy-loaded feature modules across login, home, branch search, branch config, and integrated distributor domains from the monorepo libraries. It integrates directly with three primary cloud backend APIs (Admin Assist, ERP Registration, and Distributor Onboarding) using unified NgRx state management, facades, and local storage state rehydration. The application employs the Trimble Modus design system web components to deliver a unified, highly polished, and responsive user interface.
notablePatterns: App Shell & Lazy-Loaded Features
Mediator / State Bridge (Facade of Facades)
State Rehydration & Synchronization (ngrx-store-localstorage)
Advanced RxJS Paginated Recursion (using expand and reduce in effects)
Service Dependency Injection & Overrides (via InjectionTokens)
Modus Web Components UI Architecture Integration
Client-Side Caching with Expiry (15-minute validity window check)

projects.name: admin-assist-portal-e2e
projects.purpose: This project is an end-to-end (E2E) testing suite built with Playwright for the Admin Assist Portal web application, responsible for verifying business-critical capabilities such as distributor branch search, filtering (by address, email, or status), and user authentication. Operating at the E2E application-validation layer, it simulates user flows against the deployed Angular application (and serves the application locally via nx commands when targeting localhost). Rather than being consumed by other packages, this suite targets the 'admin-assist-portal' app and integrates deeply with Azure App Configuration and Key Vault to securely resolve credentials at runtime, as well as AWS Cognito to handle automated login redirect flows.
notablePatterns: Page Object Model (POM) pattern with abstract BasePage
Worker-scoped fixtures for test isolation and shared auth state
Dynamic runtime credential resolution from Azure App Configuration and Key Vault
Cognito Hosted UI automated authentication via Angular popstate/history manipulation
Single source of truth environment-switching configurations (Local, Dev, Stg)
Token caching and validation with expiration buffers

projects.name: ai-support-assistant-app
projects.purpose: The ai-support-assistant-app is a web-based AI assistant interface designed to run as an embedded or standalone helper for Trimble desktop applications, including Accubid Classic, Accubid Anywhere, and CMS. Serving as an application shell layer, it composes shared features and utility modules into a single deployment. It coordinates authenticating with Trimble Identity (TPaaS) using query-string tokens and manages session-preserved state via NgRx Store with local storage synchronization. It loads specific AI chat-bot features using localized content and injects product-specific agent configurations extracted during route navigation.
notablePatterns: Standalone Angular components configuration bootstrapped using bootstrapApplication
Angular Signals for managing and propagating reactive state like agentName and application readiness
Custom router guard (AgentNameGuard) used to capture query parameters rather than restricting route access
NgRx state persistence in browser LocalStorage using ngrx-store-localstorage middleware
Multi-environment build setups (dev, staging, production) with index.html replacements and TPaaS OAuth configuration
Locale detection and integration using @jsverse/transloco and fallback mechanisms for regional variants like French-Canadian

projects.name: analytics-portal
projects.purpose: As an Analytics Portal in the pre-construction and estimation domain, this application enables premium manufacturers and contractors to monitor content and data usage across the Trimble ecosystem. It provides comprehensive analytics dashboards showing performance metrics for ads, content downloads, search queries, quotes, purchase requests, and 3D modeling interactions. Operating as a front-end application shell layer, it aggregates and coordinates several core features including alert management, reporting, user identity, and unauthenticated introduction modules. While it is a leaf application that isn't consumed by other projects, it composes internal workspace libraries such as `@hcworkspace/analytics-portal/data-sharing` for consent/user-relations handling and `@hcworkspace/sxui/orders/model` for data contracts. Key integration points include Trimble Identity (TID) OAuth workflows for user authentication and claims resolution, a custom licensing check system to gate premium capabilities, and embedded PowerBI client dashboards (`ngx-powerbi`) representing the core reporting mechanism.
notablePatterns: PowerBI Embedded Dashboard Integration via `ngx-powerbi` with custom filters and bookmarking features
RxJS-based Global State Management via custom services utilizing BehaviorSubjects
Trimble Identity (TID) OAuth Integration with claim-based routing and automated-testing login options
Conditional Licensing and SLA gating for Premium/Basic manufacturer features
User Consent and Data Sharing Preference Validation using internal library services

projects.name: asset-iq-portal
projects.purpose: This project acts as the primary web application portal and app shell for Trimble's Asset IQ platform. It orchestrates user-facing capabilities such as Document Parsing (for extracting and matching catalog line items) and Catalog Sharing by composing several feature modules. Operating as the application shell layer, it is responsible for global bootstrapping, layout management (header, navigation sidebar, profile drawer, and footer), and routing. It integrates directly with Trimble Platform as a Service (TPaaS) for OAuth single sign-on authentication and session management, utilizes NgRx with local storage state rehydration, and implements translation services for global localization.
notablePatterns: Web Component Integration (integrating Modus Design System web components within Angular templates for menus, navbar, side navigation, avatars, and tooltips)
State Preservation via Custom Local Storage Meta-Reducer (custom localStorageSyncReducer to rehydrate NgRx application state without losing properties on dynamically/lazy-loaded modules)
Functional Route Protection (using the canActivateWithValidAuthentication guard injected with MepAuthenticateFacade to conditionally load modules or redirect to transitions)
Environment-based Build Overrides (swapping environment.ts targets during Angular builds to manage distinct staging, development, and production endpoints)

projects.name: building-materials
projects.purpose: This project is the main application shell for the Trimble Manufacturer Content Portal (BuildingMaterials), which serves as a central hub for users to manage and process building materials files. As the app shell layer, its primary responsibility is bootstrapping the Angular application, configuring global routing, handling root state management, and defining the shared Trimble Modus Web Component layout. It does not export code for other projects to consume, but instead composes key workspace libraries including the 'file-processing' features, global authentication features, shared licensing services, and navigation features. Notable integration points include Trimble TPaaS/Trimble Identity (OIDC/OAuth2) for secure session authentication, NgRx with ngrx-store-localstorage for reactive and persistent state, and LogRocket for telemetry and exception tracking.
notablePatterns: Standalone Angular Architecture
Trimble Modus Web Components Layout Integration
Dynamic Environment-driven Configuration Injection
NgRx State Rehydration with custom metaReducers (localStorageSyncReducer, clearState)
Decoupled Navigation State Mapping Service
Centralized HTTP Interceptor for Toast Notification Errors
Exception Monitoring and Logging via LogRocket Integration

projects.name: building-materials-publications
projects.purpose: This project is the main application shell for the Building Materials Publications system, which provides users with capabilities to generate and manage material publications and estimation files. As the application shell layer, it is responsible for bootstrapping the Angular application, orchestrating global routing (including authentication/login redirection), and configuring global providers like translation engines, license validation, and state stores. Rather than being consumed by other projects, this application composes several key libraries including '@hcworkspace/building-materials-publications/file-generation/feature' for publication generation, '@hcworkspace/shared-platform-mep-authenticate-feature' for user login/logout, and shared modules for licensing and navigation. Notable integration points include state rehydration with 'ngrx-store-localstorage' for authentication state, user activity tracking with LogRocket, Trimble Identity (TPaaS) SSO integration, and Trimble Modus Web Components styling.
notablePatterns: Standalone Angular component bootstrapping via bootstrapApplication
Global HTTP interception for error toast notifications and access management
NgRx state persistence and rehydration using ngrx-store-localstorage
Trimble Modus web components integration with custom elements loader
Environment-specific token and feature flag configurations via provider factories

projects.name: csui
projects.purpose: Construction Standards UI (CSUI) is an Angular-based web application that serves as a centralized platform for managing construction MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing) standards, starting with HVAC fabrication standards (e.g., shops, materials, gauges, standards, and projects). Designed for integration with other applications or standalone use, the CSUI shell orchestrates user authentication, terms acceptance, customer selection, feature-flag evaluations, and dynamic navigation, while delegating the underlying business views to shared library components.
notablePatterns: Shell-Library Architecture with Dependency Injection Overrides (mapping shell state service implementations to generic shared library interfaces)
NgRx Effects for complex async startup and login orchestration (session, feature flags, license loading, and terms of service acceptance)
State Preservation via NgRx Meta-Reducers (using ngrx-store-localstorage with dynamic reducer update workarounds)
Dynamic Left and Top Navigation Generation based on translation keys and active routes via Factory patterns
Environment-Based Facade Configurations for endpoint overrides
Multi-Language Localization mapping browser culture languages dynamically using Transloco

projects.name: ctui
projects.purpose: A web-based Angular client application ('Workbench' or 'CraftTable') in the MEP workspace designed for contractors, estimators, detailers, and project managers to create, manage, and share assembly libraries across workflows including Estimating, Project Management, Modeling, and Fabrication.
notablePatterns: Monorepo Shell Pattern (imports core functional domains, feature views, and UI screens from shared monorepo libraries)
Dependency Inversion and Service Overrides (overrides abstract library tokens/services with shell-specific implementations like NavigationStateService and CustomAssembliesApiService)
NgRx Orchestrated Login/Licensing Workflows (uses NgRx store, actions, and effects to coordinate multi-step session acquisition, region selection, licensing, and terms of service validation)
State Persistence and Rehydration (utilizes ngrx-store-localstorage with custom meta-reducers to sync and rehydrate feature states across browser refreshes)
Standalone Angular Component Bootstrapping (uses bootstrapApplication to directly instantiate the standalone AppComponent)

projects.name: ecui
projects.purpose: The ecui project is the primary shell application for the Estimation Construct web platform, which provides Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) contractors with capabilities to manage estimates, digital engineering drawings, cost libraries, rates, and assemblies. As an application shell, it does not implement extensive custom UI components directly; rather, it coordinates global routing, navigation menus, and bootstrapping configurations, delegating specific features and data-access layers to shared workspace libraries under @hcworkspace/ecui/... and @hcworkspace/shared/.... Key modules composed by this shell include graphical takeoff, estimators, projects, work breakdown structures (WBS), drawings, and annotation/layer management. It integrates robust multi-window tab synchronization via local storage (ngrx-store-localstorage and ngx-multi-window), supports NgRx global/local state management, and utilizes LogRocket and Gainsight for usage and diagnostics tracking.
notablePatterns: App Shell Pattern: Operates as an orchestrator/shell that composes diverse workspace libraries with global routing, menus, and configurations.
State Bridge / Adapter Pattern: Implements local state/API services that extend feature-library abstract state classes to resolve circular dependencies.
Multi-Window / Multi-Tab State Sync: Utilizes ngx-multi-window and ngrx-store-localstorage to synchronize state (like scales, drawing edits) across browser windows.
Declarative Navigation Configuration: Employs factory-based definition and injection of navigation sidebar configs contextually based on active product/feature.
AOT Configuration Injection: Feeds static/runtime environment configurations dynamically using Angular custom injection tokens.

projects.name: ecui-e2e
projects.purpose: A Playwright-based end-to-end testing suite for Estimating Core User Interface (ECUI) that automates and validates workflows around Cognito authentication, cost libraries, estimates, and spreadsheet management.
notablePatterns: Worker-scoped authenticated browser contexts reusing cached Cognito session storageState to minimize login overhead
Strict locator priority favoring test-ids and user-facing semantics over fragile deep CSS selectors or XPath
Automatic environment-driven secret resolution from Azure App Configuration and Key Vault written to a gitignored resolved config
API-driven test cleanup and preparation using Playwright APIRequestContext to bypass slow user interface workflows
Stateful best-effort resource tracking via local JSON (.runtime-ids.json) for global teardown execution
Web-first assertions polling UI states and loaders/spinners instead of hardcoded timers or page.waitForTimeout
Collision avoidance through timestamp-and-random-suffix based run ID generation

projects.name: electricaldomain
projects.purpose: The electricaldomain application serves as the main application shell and entry point for Trimble's MEP electrical design system, orchestrating multiple feature modules to deliver user-facing capabilities such as electrical network planning, load calculations, single-line diagrams, and cable/supply/protective device configurations. As the app shell layer, its primary responsibilities include root-level routing, loading domain-specific configurations, and bootstrapping the application using Trimble's Modus Web Components and design system. It composes various domain feature and data-access libraries, loading their configurations dynamically from environment-specific endpoints. Key integration points include Trimble's TPaaS identity service for OAuth authorization, desktop webview bridges via WebViewService, Gainsight analytics, and telemetry/logging using LogRocket integrated directly with the NgRx store.
notablePatterns: Environment-driven multi-module configuration injection using specialized data-access config models
State-based orchestration using NgRx store/effects coupled with LogRocket telemetry middleware
Dual-mode authentication strategy supporting both web-based OAuth (TPaaS) and external desktop webview token handshakes

Modular, path-aliased monorepo library consumption separating core features from data-access layers

projects.name: fabui
projects.purpose: The fabui project is an Angular-based application that serves as the main web user interface (app shell) for the fabrication management domain (Corsa). It provides business capabilities for managing and editing fabrication projects, creating and tracking work packages, managing assemblies, visualizing 3D models, and interacting with detached bill of materials (BOM) panels. As the top-level application shell, it is not consumed by other packages, but instead composes key functional, authentication, and user interface libraries from the @hcworkspace namespace. Key integration points include real-time project model updates via a SignalR ModelsHub, conversational assistance via an integrated AI Assistant panel, TPaaS authentication with custom session-state restoration, and on-demand Trimble Modus Design System component preloading.
notablePatterns: Custom sessionStorage restoration and token context replication from opener window to handle multi-window detached workflows (Detached BOM)
On-demand preloading of Trimble Modus Web Components (modus-wc-*) on browser idle callback (requestIdleCallback) or on initialization
Reactive navigation layout state integration with feature flags and translation data using combineLatest
Debounced and minimum-duration route loading state transitions (150ms start debounce and 500ms minimum display times) to avoid layout flickering
Meta-reducer local storage synchronization (localStorageSync) for state persistence of authenticated sessions
API configuration dependency injection via factory providers, mapping environment parameters dynamically

projects.name: fabui-design
projects.purpose: The `fabui-design` (also known as Corsa FAB UI) application provides a modern, responsive user interface for project management, workshop configuration, work packages, shop floor planning, and bill of materials (BOM) tracking in the fabrication domain. Serving as the primary application shell layer, it orchestrates overall layout, global themes, and routing while composing multiple modular feature libraries. It relies on the custom `@hcworkspace/fabui-design/ui-components` library for pure Angular replacement components (Modusy) mapping to Trimble Modus 2.0 Web Components, alongside other platform components like `@hcworkspace/shared-platform-mep-authenticate-feature`. Notable integration points include native NgRx states with local storage synchronization, localized date formatting using browser locales, dynamic theme synchronization with DevExtreme controls, and deep integration with Trimble Connect APIs for 3D model viewing.
notablePatterns: Facade Pattern (NgRx State Management encapsulation via Facades)
Modusy Component Wrapper Architecture (Pure Angular component replacements for Trimble Modus 2.0 Web Components)
Signal-Based State Management (Native Angular 18 signals for local component state)
Adaptive & Responsive Layout Detection (@HostListener window resizing with custom breakpoints)
LocalStorage State Synchronization (ngrx-store-localstorage for persistent session token management)
Opener-Aware/Detached Window Session Restoration (FabuiDesignSessionRestoreService for popped-out 3D viewer pages)
Dynamic Feature Flags & Visibility Presets Engine (FeatureVisibilityService for runtime visibility configuration)
Synchronized Theme Injections (ThemeService coupled with DevExtremeThemeService dynamic stylesheet creation)

projects.name: fmsconnect
projects.purpose: The fmsconnect project provides integration of Trimble Connect's File Management System (FMS) with the Accubid Anywhere Desktop application, allowing desktop-launched webviews to view and manage project files. It operates as an App Shell layer, composing core authentication and file management features into a lightweight Angular application optimized for desktop integration. The application composes the lazy-loaded feature module @hcworkspace/fmsconnect/feature and utilizes the data-access library @hcworkspace/shared-platform-mep-authenticate-data-access. It relies heavily on query parameter login guards to extract tokens and project identifiers from the desktop shell, bridging them with Trimble Identity (TPaaS) SSO and local state persistence via NgRx.
notablePatterns: Query parameter interception for desktop/webview shell auth
State service delegation implementing shared lazy-loaded interfaces
State persistence and rehydration meta-reducer via localStorageSync
SSO routing orchestration with Trimble Identity TPaaS
HTTP Interceptor token injection for micro-frontend shells

projects.name: hangers
projects.purpose: The hangers application is a Trimble MEP client-side application designed to manage engineering calculations and design workflows for structural hangers and supports. Acting as an application shell layer, it bootstraps the Angular framework, configures global services, and composes key features from underlying libraries such as HangersDataAccessModule from @hcworkspace/hangers/data-access. It integrates a web-to-desktop browser bridge via DotNetRequestMessageService to communicate with a .NET host application, such as fetching user interface language preferences. Notable integration points include connections to the external Trimble Network Calculations REST API, DevExtreme license validation, and NgRx state management initialization.
notablePatterns: Web-to-Desktop Browser Bridge for dynamic host-to-client configuration
Dynamic internationalization mapping from .NET host language codes to standard locales
Third-party component library (DevExtreme) license validation at root bootstrap
Application shell architecture delegating UI rendering to library elements like <mep-hangers-shell>
Global NgRx state and effects initialization at the application root module
Dependency injection of environment-specific API endpoints using provider tokens

projects.name: hangers-e2e
projects.purpose: End-to-end (E2E) testing of a Hanger configuration and placement web interface, verifying element selection options, standard presets (e.g., DIN standards), spacing tables, and interactive UI behaviors.
notablePatterns: Page Object Model (POM) to encapsulate DevExtreme UI locators and user actions

projects.name: hcui
projects.purpose: hcui (Honeycomb UI) serves as the primary application shell and host frontend for Trimble's Estimating platform, which provides Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) estimating and graphical takeoff capabilities. It integrates and composes countless modular libraries for managing projects, estimates, 2D/3D drawing viewers, annotation tools, and supplier/distributor pricing. The application orchestrates global authentication flows, licensing checks, multi-window events, and telemetry integrations (LogRocket and Gainsight/Aptrinsic), while defining lazy-loaded routing structures and managing high-level application state. This host layer coordinates business logic across distinct domain libraries through unified NgRx state management and custom facade integrations.
notablePatterns: Facade Pattern & NgRx State Orchestration: Decoupling feature components from backend services and NgRx details through domain-specific facades like OrchestrationFacade and EstimatesFacade.

State Adapter Extension Pattern: Creating local wrapper services in the host app (such as SharedAnnotationStateService) that extend the abstract feature state service classes defined in shared libraries to supply concrete store facades and reactive streams.
Modular Lazy Loading: Composing routes and loading domain libraries on-demand across dozens of workspace feature packages with dedicated functional activation guards.
Environment-based Feature Toggling: Distributing feature toggles dynamically via the environments config and angular guards to control layout features and third-party integrations.
State Sanitization: Intercepting and cleaning NgRx developer tool history logs using stateSanitizer functions to exclude credentials and performance-heavy payloads.

projects.name: hcui-e2e
projects.purpose: This project is the end-to-end (E2E) testing suite for the Estimating MEP/MEP Estimating UI application ('hcui'). Operating as an external validation and test automation layer, it ensures the functionality and regression resistance of key workflows, including project and estimate creation, drawing uploads/scale calibration, favorites management, and complex takeoff operations (Trade Service, custom libraries, assemblies, and Fabric.js canvas-based graphical takeoffs). Rather than being consumed by other applications, it orchestrates and exercises the 'hcui' Angular web client and integrates directly with Trimble MEP Platform Services and Trimble Connect via REST APIs. Notable integration points include Cognito for identity and login management, Azure App Configuration and Key Vault for credential resolution, and real-time canvas coordination for Fabric.js drawing annotation.
notablePatterns: Page Object Model (POM) extending BasePage with explicit direct navigation restrictions
Worker-scoped login context (loggedInContext) preserving active Angular/NgRx state across tests in a worker
Web-first actionability checks (visible, stable, enabled polling) using Playwright locator hierarchy to ban sleep/waitForTimeout
Direct API-driven testing and resource cleanup alongside UI flows using Playwright APIRequestContext
Environment-wide resource seeding (e.g. drawings/scales) combined with robust main-process global teardown to prevent orphan accumulation
Credential resolution from Azure App Configuration and Key Vault via ConfigurationHelper
Inter-test UI recovery and sanitization (sanitiseAfterTest) to reset shared state between runs

projects.name: livecount
projects.purpose: This project acts as the primary Angular application shell for the Trimble LiveCount estimating and visual takeoff solution within the MEP (mechanical, electrical, plumbing) workspace. It provides contractors and estimators with the ability to manage construction jobs, view drawings and blueprint designs, perform 2D and 3D quantity takeoffs, make annotations, and utilize AI-powered auto-counting tools. The application shell coordinates routing, bootstraps the Angular framework configuration, manages global top-bar/sidebar layouts, and handles session and localization setup. It composes a wide range of workspace libraries covering estimating, drawings, scales, models, and platform integrations like LogRocket, Gainsight, and Trimble Connect Projects.
notablePatterns: Interface State Redirection (Adapter Pattern): Employs specific local service adapters (e.g., NavigationStateService, SharedAnnotationStateService) inside apps/livecount to implement platform feature contracts/tokens. It resolves and routes abstract feature actions down to concrete Ngrx state facades or platform-level APIs.

Dynamic Feature and License Configured Providers: Registers functional configurations through factories (such as provideSharedGraphicalTakeoffConfig) that evaluate active feature flags, regional parameters, and license SKU types to toggle layout settings, AI features, and user capabilities on-the-fly.

Multi-Tab Synchronized Store State: Listens to the window's local storage events to dispatch a Storage synchronizing action, keeping multiple browser tabs cleanly aligned and synchronized on the same global NgRx state tree.

Embedded WebView / Desktop Host Integration: Includes special login flows (such as LiveCountEmbedLoginComponent) and real-time messaging services (LiveCountMessageFacade) to connect with webview bridges for seamlessly embedding the web app inside classic native desktop hosts.

Unified Performance and Event Tracking: Directly orchestrates LogRocket, Gainsight analytics (Aptrinsic), and customized Error handlers across application bootstraps and layout states for central session diagnostics.

projects.name: livecount-studio
projects.purpose: This project, livecount-studio, is an administrative utility and developer dashboard for managing, testing, and debugging the LiveCount estimating platform. It serves as an application shell that compiles various management workflows, allowing authorized developers and administrators to manage jobs, copy drawing data, migrate customer annotation layers, and delete customer offboarding data. It coordinates integrations with Trimble Identity (TID) for OAuth access, legacy and internal LiveCount REST APIs, and provides real-time interaction with the LiveCount viewer using both embedded iframes and SignalR. The app is a standalone utility that composes these API connections and iframe viewers into an interactive administrative dashboard.

Bi-directional iframe postMessage communication with embedded LiveCount viewer
Real-time notifications integration via jQuery SignalR client (LiveCountSignalrApi)

Experiment-Agentic-Flow/quantitytakeoffs.purpose: The Quantity Takeoff Service resides within the MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing) Estimation platform and solves the challenge of extracting, versioning, and managing material quantities from 3D building models (Trimble Connect files) for web-based estimation tools. It is primarily invoked by frontend applications via REST endpoints like Connect3DModelController, QuantityTakeoffItemController, ManualTakeoffController, and ChangesetController to publish browser-ingested takeoff data, track user edit history (changesets), and manage manual records. Additionally, other platform components interact with the service asynchronously via MassTransit over Azure Service Bus, triggering message consumers such as DeleteModelsConsumer or SaveTakeoffEntryConsumer to handle complex, multi-service workflows. The service's core capabilities include 3D model lifecycle management, version-aware takeoff data ingestion, manual takeoff CRUD, changeset revision tracking, and real-time client notifications powered by SignalR. Architecturally, it depends upstream on Trimble Connect (via TrimbleFileService) for file storage, Azure Key Vault for AES encryption, and Azure App Configuration; downstream, it coordinates with an external Annotation Service using the MassTransit Courier Routing Slip pattern to guarantee transactional integrity when modifying estimate records and annotations.

CourierActivities (Distributed saga execution steps for routing slips)
SignalR (QuantityTakeoffHub for pushing real-time status updates)
Services (Trimble file access, AES encryption, data protection, and DB indexing)
dependencies: Annotation Service (downstream collaborator via Routing Slip activities)
Customer Data Hub (CDH - GDPR/deletion event publisher)
notablePatterns: Routing Slip Pattern (MassTransit Courier for coordinated, multi-service transactions)

Experiment-Agentic-Flow/quantitytakeoffo.purpose: The Quantity Takeoff Orchestrator Service belongs to the MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing) Estimation domain and functions as the asynchronous workflow engine for LiveCount's 3D Quantity Takeoff feature. The service is triggered asynchronously via Azure Service Bus message contracts, where upstream components or services publish an `IProcessTrimBimModel` message to initiate the 3D model conversion pipeline. Client applications also connect directly to its Azure SignalR hub (`/quantitytakeoffhub`) to join a specific notification group and receive real-time stage-by-stage updates of the conversion progress, while the Merlin Customer Data Hub (CDH) calls it via `DeleteComponentCdhRequestMessage` to handle customer data purging for GDPR compliance. Its core capabilities include downloading and parsing TrimBim (.trb) models from Trimble Connect, extracting 3D element metadata and property set definitions (PSets) in a memory-efficient streamed manner, generating and compressing a gzipped JSON output of these elements, uploading the output files to Trimble File Service, and storing the extracted property metadata and file references into a MongoDB database. In the broader architecture, this service acts as the backend processor supporting the REST-based QuantityTakeoffService, calling out to Trimble Connect APIs, interacting with Azure Key Vault for token cryptography, integrating with Trimble File Service for storage, and publishing completion and failure events to Azure Service Bus to notify downstream consumers.
notablePatterns: Saga State Machine Pattern (MassTransit state machine with MongoDB persistence)
Publish-Subscribe / Asynchronous Messaging (MassTransit + Azure Service Bus)
Event-Driven Real-time Updates (broadcasting state changes to groups via Azure SignalR Hub)
Repository Pattern (decoupling data persistence in MongoDB)
Processor-Repository Separation (encapsulating orchestration, business logic, and data access)
Stream-based Serialization & Compression (using FileStream and GZipStream to mitigate memory exhaustion)
